Thursday, September 17, 2026

International News · 16 Sources · 4 Regions

Daily Brief

The US Federal Reserve raised interest rates for the first time in over three years, hiking to 3.75%-4% despite fierce opposition from President Trump, who nonetheless expressed support for Fed Chair Kevin Warsh while calling the board 'hostile' [BBC, France 24, Nikkei Asia]. The decision sent Asian currencies weakening against the dollar, with the yen slipping to the 156-range. In Europe, Commission President Ursula von der Leyen proposed making Canada the EU's first associate member, drawing an immediate threat of tariffs from Trump who called the plan 'laughable' and potentially 'hostile' [RFI, France 24, Le Monde]. The EU also announced sweeping restrictions on social media access for under-15s through the proposed EU Kids Act, which would ban under-13s from platforms entirely and limit teens aged 13-15 to one hour daily via parental 'mini accounts' [BBC]. In Paris, France hosted security talks with Lebanon and Jordan on replacing the UN's UNIFIL peacekeeping mission in southern Lebanon as its mandate nears expiration [RFI, Al Jazeera, Le Monde, France 24]. Meanwhile, South African authorities are investigating the discovery of a ninth woman's body near Johannesburg in two months, with President Ramaphosa vowing that 'no stone will be left unturned' amid growing fears of serial killings [BBC, The Guardian].

Top Stories
01 Economics

Federal Reserve Raises Interest Rates Despite Trump Opposition, Citing Persistent Inflation

  • The Federal Reserve unanimously raised rates to 3.75%-4% from 3.5%-3.75%, the first increase in over three years
  • Fed Chair Kevin Warsh said the move was necessary because 'inflation is too high and has been for too long,' noting US inflation has exceeded the 2% target for more than five years
  • President Trump had called for rate cuts but expressed support for Warsh after the decision while calling the Fed board 'hostile'
  • Asian currencies weakened following the announcement, with the Japanese yen falling to the 156-range against the dollar

02 Geopolitics

EU Proposes Canada as First Associate Member, Drawing Trump Tariff Threat

  • European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen proposed making Canada the EU's first associate member during her State of the Union speech, with Canadian PM Mark Carney in attendance
  • Von der Leyen suggested closer cooperation on tech, defense, and energy as democracies face a 'fracture in the international rules-based system'
  • Trump called the proposal 'laughable' and threatened 'very serious tariffs or stop trading with Europe' if he considers it a 'hostile act'
  • The European Commission responded that the alliance plan is 'not against anyone' but for both parties' common strengths

03 Policy

EU Announces Plan to Restrict Social Media Access for Children Under 15

  • The proposed EU Kids Act would ban children under 13 from accessing social media platforms entirely
  • Children aged 13-15 would be limited to one hour per day via 'mini accounts' set up through parents' accounts
  • Social media companies would need to prove platforms are 'safe by design' or face fines of up to 6% of global sales
  • The restrictions would apply to TikTok, Instagram, Snapchat, YouTube, AI chatbots, and online games

04 Geopolitics

France Hosts Security Talks on Replacing UN Peacekeeping Mission in Lebanon

  • French President Macron met with Lebanese President Joseph Aoun and Jordan's King Abdullah II to discuss post-UNIFIL security arrangements
  • The UN peacekeeping mission UNIFIL's mandate ends this year after nearly half a century of operations dating back to 1978
  • France and Italy have proposed a multinational coalition to succeed UNIFIL and prevent a security vacuum in southern Lebanon
  • Israeli forces continue to occupy what Israel calls a 'security zone' in southern Lebanon despite a framework deal agreed in June

05 Society

South Africa Investigates Ninth Woman's Body Found Near Johannesburg Amid Serial Killing Fears

  • Police confirmed discovery of a ninth woman's body in two months, found half-naked and wrapped in a sheet in Dawn Park on Thursday
  • Eight women's bodies have been found since July across Ekurhuleni, near Johannesburg's OR Tambo international airport
  • Several victims were found partially clothed with injuries; police have not confirmed whether the deaths are connected or if a serial killer is responsible
  • President Ramaphosa vowed 'no stone will be left unturned' as the killings cause 'fear and uncertainty in our communities'
